chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Jahm, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him), 'Which of the two is superior: staying in Makkah or staying in Al-Medina?' He said, 'What do you say?' I said, 'And what is my word compared to your word?' He said, 'Your word returns you to my word.' So I said to him, 'As for me, I claim that staying in Al-Medina is superior to staying in Makkah.' He said, 'Indeed, if you say that, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said that on the day of Fitr. He went to Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and greeted him in the Masjid, then said: 'We have been preferred over the people today by our greeting Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'
ai.seo_question: Which city is considered superior for staying, Makkah or Al-Medah, according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Rida (AS) validates the superiority of residing in Medina over Mecca by linking it to the specific virtue of greeting the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) there, a practice highlighted on Eid al-Fitr. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the spiritual merit of the Prophet's burial place and the continuity of his presence through the Ahl al-Bayt's reverence for Medina. The dialogue illustrates the method of *taqlid* (following the Imam's lead) while allowing for independent reasoning, as Al-Hasan's initial guess aligns with the Imam's deeper theological stance.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al Hassan Bin Jahm who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Which of the two is superior, the staying in Makkah or in Al-Medina?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Which thing are you saying?’ So I said, ‘And what is my word (compared) with your<sup>asws</sup> word?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Your words would return you to my<sup>asws</sup> words’. So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I claim that the staying in Al-Medina is superior than staying in Al-Makkah’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But, although you said that, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said that (as well) on the day of Fitr, and he<sup>asws</sup> went over to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> greeted to him<sup>saww</sup> in the Masjid, then said: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> have been preferred over the people today by our<sup>asws</sup> sending greetings upon Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from al-Hassan ibn Jahm who has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Is staying in Makkah more virtuous or in al- Madinah?’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘What do you say about it?’ I (the narrator) replied, ‘My words are not of any significance before your words.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Your words return you to my words.’ I (the narrator) then said, ‘I believe staying in al-Madinah is more virtuous than in Makkah.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘What you said is the same as what abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said on a day of ‘Id al-Fitr during his visit of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause. He offered his al-Salam in the Masjid and said, ‘We today have been given preference over people due to our offering al-Salam to the Messenger of Allah.’”
